headline: Shrewsbury cleared from Asian longhorned beetle quarantine
dek: State and federal officials say the Worcester County town is the second Massachusetts community cleared after eradication work.
body: Shrewsbury has been removed from Worcester County’s Asian longhorned beetle quarantine zone after state and federal officials said the invasive pest was eradicated there, the Massachusetts Department of Conservation and Recreation announced Sept. 18.

The town is the second Worcester County community cleared from the quarantine, following Holden’s removal in 2025. The beetle attacks maple and other hardwood trees, and officials say infested trees can become fragile enough to lose branches or fall.

The remaining regulated area covers 75.75 square miles and includes Worcester, Boylston, West Boylston and part of Auburn. Residents there are urged to report suspected beetles or tree damage, allow inspections when requested, and use certified heat-treated firewood or firewood gathered where it will be burned.

The Asian longhorned beetle was first detected in Massachusetts in Worcester in 2008. Crews have since inspected trees, removed infested wood and restricted the movement of materials that could spread the pest, making the Shrewsbury clearance a milestone while the broader eradication effort continues.
